system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Buyer-side advice; the Seller's materials have been treated as counterparty drafts, not as instructions or agreed positions.

## Preliminary observation

The Seller Update repeatedly describes positions as "addressed", "agreed", "settled", "considered adequate" or "evidenced". None of these are confirmed through our authority process, and several are directly contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (notably Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay). Under playbook sec 0.4/6.3 we should not accept any characterisation as agreed. Two of the Seller's numbers (20% cap; 18-month period) happen to match our *conditional fallbacks*. That is not clearance: no written authority from Amelia Frost exists for either, so our response must hold the starting positions.

---

## A. Liability regime – departures from playbook

| Topic | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority | **Reject.** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not move to 20% without written authority identifying this draft. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject** – 5x our position. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar (tipping) | **Reject.** Two departures: quantum (5x) and structure (deductible vs tipping). The deductible is the more valuable point to win. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost approval | **Reject.** Counter at 24 months. |
| **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Blanket override | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject outright.** This single sentence would sweep fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, tax, IP, leakage/payment claims and covenants into the general cap, basket and 18-month window. Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. |
| **Fundamental/Title** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime; 100% cap; ≥6 years; outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. A title failure means we have not bought the company; a 20% cap on that is unacceptable. |
| **Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"** | Universal application | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | **Reject.** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. This is a non-negotiable for us; it must be added expressly and expressed to apply to the maximum extent enforceable. The non-reliance clause should also not purport to exclude liability for fraudulent misrepresentation. |

**Reasoning:** The combined effect of the Seller's package is a general cap at AUD 4.8m, a hard deductible of AUD 250k, an 18-month window, and – via the "all Claims" language – the collapse of every other claim category into that regime, with no fraud exception. On a AUD 24m deal that is materially below our floor on every axis and, in the fraud and fundamental-warranty respects, below what we can accept on any authority.

## B. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure.** The Seller deems disclosed the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Playbook: specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. **Reject.** Require a disclosure standard (fair, specific, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter) and limit general disclosure, if any, to the Disclosure Letter itself and identified Accounts.

**Cl 8.3 – buyer knowledge exclusion.** "No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." **Reject.** This is a blanket, constructive-knowledge exclusion extending to advisers and to matters merely "discoverable". It would make the warranties close to worthless and double-counts with the general disclosure. Playbook: delete; any knowledge qualifier must be confined to actual knowledge of named buyer persons, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Note [1.4] of the Disclosure Letter also denies that anything disclosed is a matter requiring consent, payment, notification or remediation – a reservation we should not treat as substantive.

## C. Conditions, completion mechanics and specific issues

**1. Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) – material.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller Update says consent is "addressed" with reasonable endeavours and deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. The Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms that **no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied** has been provided. Playbook: effective consent *and* evidence of satisfaction of conditions before Completion; delivery alone is insufficient; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer. **Push back:** make it a hard condition precedent – unconditional written consent (or consent whose conditions are demonstrably satisfied) in agreed form, with a Seller obligation to procure (not merely use endeavours), plus a no-adverse-change-in-Bluefen-relationship bring-down and a walk right if not satisfied by the long-stop date.

**2. Riverlark (cl 2/7) – material.** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; Seller proposes a release "following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge of security. Playbook: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. **Push back:** require a dated payout figure, deduction and direct payment from the purchase price at Completion, and executed releases/ASIC discharge deliverables on the Completion agenda. A post-Completion release is only tolerable with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval; neither exists. Also check clause 8.1 change-of-control – the bank's consent/payout should be a condition.

**3. Employee bonuses (DD-005 – AUD 420,000) – material to price.** The Seller says bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" yet the funds flow omits them. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms omission and is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs. Because the bonuses are triggered by Completion and paid by the Company post-Completion, silence means the Buyer effectively funds them. **Push back:** either (a) specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price (bonus + superannuation + payroll tax + any other on-costs), or (b) Seller-funded with a specific indemnity and gross-up. Insist the funds flow is not "agreed price mechanics" – it is incomplete.

**4. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).** The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it adequate. Disclosure Letter para 4 confirms clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables. **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover failure of IP ownership/transfer in the SOW3 materials and any third-party claims, preserve the cure (payment and written confirmatory assignment pre-Completion as a Completion deliverable), and obtain independent verification of the payment status. Do not accept AUD 180,000 as the measure either way.

**5. Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** The Seller labels it "preliminary, not expected to be material". Disclosure para 6 is consistent with our own understanding: ~1,240 records, unknown access, unknown scope, notification not determined. Playbook: assume no confirmed breach, no harm and no numeric demand in either direction. **Position:** no price adjustment now, but require (a) log preservation and completion of the investigation, (b) ongoing updates and a bring-down at Completion, (c) a specific indemnity for losses, notification costs and regulatory consequences arising from the incident, sitting outside the general cap/basket. Do not let the "not expected to be material" characterisation migrate into the SPA.

**6. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure para 8 is honest that it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Playbook: assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. **Action:** DD follow-up on timing, termination rights and accrual treatment in the locked-box/completion accounts; reserve position. Not a headline pushback today.

**7. Tax / IP warranties.** Seller: "settled under the general regime". Playbook: OPEN; no unlimited liability but no resolution. **Reject the characterisation.** Tax and IP must be separate categories with their own cap and period (tax typically to the statutory review period plus margin). Do not accept them being folded into the 20%/18-month regime.

**8. Title.** Seller: title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. The Disclosure Letter itself (para 10) concedes this is merely the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it. Playbook: DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. **Action:** obtain independent ASIC searches, PPSR searches against Seller and Company, constitution and any shareholder agreement, board/shareholder authority evidence, and warranty/indemnity that shares are fully paid, unencumbered and that no rights to acquire exist. Riverlark's security is a live encumbrance point here.

**9. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** Both appear to be notification/assignment provisions not triggered by a share sale. Low priority; confirm by reading the clauses rather than relying on the Seller's gloss, and include notification as a post-Completion covenant where needed.

---

## D. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable / escalate if resisted**
1. Insert an express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
2. Delete "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" and the extension of cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 to "Claims of any nature". Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
3. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
4. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion.
5. Replace general data-room/public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure.

**Hold starting positions (no authority to move)**
6. Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m; de minimis AUD 5,000; tipping basket AUD 50,000; 24-month general period. Record internally that the Seller's 20%/18-month figures coincide with our fallbacks but are **not** cleared – seek Amelia Frost's written instruction before any movement.

**Conditions and mechanics**
7. Bluefen: hard CP – effective consent plus evidence conditions satisfied, pre-Completion.
8. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion.
9. DD-005 bonuses: specific funds-flow line (with on-costs) or Seller-funded with indemnity.
10. Ironquay: broaden indemnity to IP ownership; SOW3 payment and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverable; verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
11. DD-006: specific indemnity outside the general regime; investigation, log preservation and updates; no price move now.

**Keep open / DD follow-up**
12. Tax and IP warranty terms remain open with separate regimes – reject "settled".
13. Title: independent verification package; do not rely on DD-012.
14. Sandbar renewals and lease/Mossvale: assess; no automatic adjustment.

**Drafting response:** Our mark-up should reject the Seller's framing sentence by sentence rather than accept the "fair and balanced package" premise. Where the Seller's own Disclosure Letter undercuts the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, title), cite it back to them.
=== END ADVICE ===
